note: v1, FIRST DRAFT of the closer, 'Still Running When You Wake' (6:10, 186 bars, 112 -> 126 bpm on a tempo map). An orchestra of illusions that GROWS LIKE A PLANT: an L-system (A -> AB, B -> A, the Fibonacci word, with one mutation per generation - every k-th A becomes C) plays one generation per section and is at once the melody (A a step up, B two down, C a leap), the rhythm (eighth, dotted eighth, sixteenth: quasi-periodic, a loop that never quite repeats), the walk of the harmony and the form (sections 8 5 8 13 21 34 13 55 21 8 bars: the piece grows from one note and ends on one note). TUNING 31-EDO as fractional MIDI: a 'neutral Dorian' on F# (F# G# neutral-third B C# D# E); chords of 6/5 minors, harmonic sevenths (7/4), neutral thirds - measured: the celesta's whole tone at 5.03 steps of 31-EDO (195 cents), not 12-TET's 200. Line-up: a music box (the light) over a fan's hum; celesta, kalimba, harp with SYMPATHETIC strings; bowed cellos and violins (and violins doubling the lead in g6); a horn section (lips) answering the harmonic-seventh chords; a PHANTOM bass nobody plays and a real sub in the peaks; machine-kit drums with drunk hats and late claps; a SHEPARD choir rising for ever through g5 and a Shepard fall through the prune; a BARBER POLE on the prune's strings; WARP drifting the hats a sixteenth and back; a RISSET rush through the coda that keeps accelerating and never gets faster. Seeds 0/11: 93.72 / 93.72 (spectrum 60, cohesion 60 - next round); levels clean (-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 1); render ~0.26 of real time.
next: Spectrum and cohesion (60): find the bands; a humanized voice (obtuse words, low in the mix); glide/bend/expression paths on the lead; the seed's light as the album's first note.

note: v8 (judgment keep, -0.37; a meter change - unused on the album - where it means something): THE PRUNE IS PRUNED. Bars 90-102, where the L-system is cut back before the last growth, are now in 7/8: every bar loses an eighth (a tempo-map meter point), a hitch in the breath under 'count the leaves again'; g6 grows back into full 4/4. Taught plainly: the prune, which had no drums, now COUNTS - a rimshot on every eighth, seven to a bar grouped 2+2+3, downbeat accented - so the missing eighth is heard, while the cello and Shepard chords re-strike every three and a half beats. Engineering: the generator still composes in virtual 4/4 and warps at output (rb/warp: a pruned bar's last eighth is dropped, everything after shifts; the spoken lines move with their bar), so no part needed rewriting; the song is 2.2 s shorter. Two metric notes, honestly: compscore's rhythm grid is the tempo map's MEDIAN bpm, so a linear 122.97 bpm at the new point moved the grid 121 -> 123 and read the closer as metronomic (94.4); and a meter-only point (no bpm) made the engine hold 118 until bar 90, flattening g4-g5's rise. So the point carries 121: 118 -> 121 by the prune, 121 -> 124 through it (at most 2 bpm off the line; the prune quickens a little as it is cut). Seeds 0/11 (v7 98.24 / 98.19): 97.87 / 97.83; rhythm 96.7 / 95.7 (off-grid share 0.09-0.10, the band's edge); levels clean (-11.1 LUFS, TP -1.29).
